Md Mustaque Ahmed with Sayda Rofika Khatun, Advocates—For the Petitioner. 
Rezaul Karim with Mohammad Samiul Huq, Advocates—For the Opposite Party Nos. 1-4.
parties:
Younus Miah (Md) ------ Plaintiff-Respondent-Petitioner
Vs
Jarip Ali and others  ------ Defendants-Appellants-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-4, to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 19-1-2017 (decree signed on 24-1-2017), passed by the Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Chattogram, in Other Appeal No.517 of 2011, allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 24-8-2011 (decree signed on 29-8-2011), passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Rangunia, Chattogram, in Other Suit No. 94 of 2004 decreeing the suit, should not be set-aside and/or pass such other order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that, one Md Younus Miah, as plaintiff, had filed Other Suit No. 94 of 2004 before the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Rangunia, Chattogram, against the defendants-appellants-opposite parties seeking permanent injunction in respect of the suit property measuring 0.1102 acres of land as mentioned in the schedule to the plaint.

3. The defendant Nos. 1-4 had appeared and contested in that suit by filing written statements on 25-10-2004. The plaintiff examined one PW and defendants have also examined 2 DWs in support their respective cases.

4. However, the trial court, after hearing the parties and assessing the evidence on record, decreed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 24-8-2011 (decree signed on 29-8-2011).

5. Against the said judgment and decree of the trial court, the defendants preferred Other Appeal No.517 of 2011 before the District Judge, Chattogram, which was heard by the Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Chattogram, who being the Appellate Court, has passed the impugned judgment and decree, allowing the appeal by setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court, vide judgment and decree dated 19-1-2017 (decree signed on 24-1-2017).

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 19-1-2017 (decree signed on 24-1-2017) of the Appellate Court the plaintiff-respondent-petitioner has filed this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule.

7. Learned Advocates Mr Md Mostaque Ahmed and Mrs. Sayeda Rofika Khatun appeared for the petitioner. Mr Ahmed, having placed the petition and other materials on record, first of all submits that, the plaintiff has proved his possession in the suit property being present before the court as PW 1. Besides, the plaintiff has also filed some documents marked as exhibit 3 and 4 which shows that, the plaintiff had a grocery shop on the suit plot and that he had a nationality certificate, issued by the Chairman of the No. 1 Rajanagar Union Parishad on 20-3-2008 (Exhibit 4), showing Bochan Ali, as father of the plaintiff Md Younus Miah. As such, he submits that, the plaintiff has been able to prove his title by an oral gift made by his foster mother Albela Khatun and that he was in possession of the suit property. He further submits that, this being a suit for permanent injunction, the plaintiff has proved his prima-facie title and exclusive possession in the suit property and that in such a case, the court need not have to decide the disputed question of title. In support of his contention, he has referred to the decision reported in 56 DLR (AD) 22: between Jobayer Hossain vs Noor Hafez. Accordingly, he maintains that, the trial court has rightly passed the judgment and decree in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner. But, the appellate court has utterly failed to appreciate the legal aspects of this case and the evidence on record and, out of full misconception of law, it has passed the impugned judgment and decree and, as such, this Rule has merit and the same may kindly be made absolute.

8. Learned Advocates Mr Rezaul Karim and Mr Mohammad Samiul Huq appeared on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1-4. The first contention of the learned Advocate Mr Huq is that, the case of the plaintiff Md Younus Miah, PW 1 has not been corroborated by any other competent witness. The learned Advocates pointed out that, during cross-examination of PW I (the sole-witness) he has admitted that Albela Khatun was alive, but he could not make the said Albela Khatun was present before the court as witness to prove the oral gift allegedly made by her in his favour or to support his possession by making a shop on the suit property. Mr Huq next also submits that, the plaintiff possessed the suit property and the certificate issued by the concerned Chairman, No. 1 Rajanagar Union Parishad on 20-3-2008, which can easily be procured by managing the local Chairman of a Union Parishad and this not a proof of alleged gift or of possession. He next pointed out that, during examination of PW 1 he has admitted that —“না: দাগে বিবাদীদের ঘর-বাড়ি চিনি।” The learned Advocates next submits that, the appellate court has rightly held that, the plaintiff (petitioner) did neither call, nor produce Albela Khatun as witness to prove his case. The appellate court has also recorded that, at the time of alleged oral gift and handing over of possession on 15-1-1974, Bochan Ali, Naderuzzaman, Kabir Ahmed and Bodiul Alam were allegedly present. But having examined the record of Other Suit No. 94 of 2004, it appears that, the plaintiff did not call or examine any one of them as witness to prove the fact of handing over of the possession as asserted by him. On the contrary, the appellate court also recorded that, the defendants' case, that they have acquired the suit property from Albela Khatun on the basis of a registered sale deed No. 573 dated 17-3-2004 (Exhibit-Kha) has not been challenged, nor claimed that deed to be a forged deed/documents created by the plaintiff. Besides, the appellate court has also recorded the deposition of DW 2, who is the attesting witness No. 3 of the aforesaid sale deed No. 573 dated 17-3-2004 (Exhibit-Kha). On these basis, the appellate court has found title and possession of the defendant in the suit property and held that, the findings of the trial court were not based on proper appreciation of evidence on record. Hence, the appellate court has set-aside the findings of the trial court. The appellate court has also held that, no one can, in the absence of any lawful title, claim permanent injunction in the suit property, nor anyone having entered into the suit property on the basis of any oral license can deny or refuse to hand over the possession of the suit property as has been claimed by the plaintiff. The appellate court has finally found that, the defendants' had no legal interest in the suit property. The appellate court has, I find, righty set-aside the judgment of the trial court, the learned Advocate continues. Finally, the learned Advocates for the OP Nos. 1- 4 referred to the decision, reported in the case of Md Kamal vs AKM Mohsin, 10 MLR (AD) 100 in which, the Apex Court held that, in a suit for permanent injunction, if the dispute involves complicated question of title the plaintiff must establish his title by filing a regular suit for declaration of title. A simple suit for permanent injunction should not be allowed to be used as a testing devise for ascertainment of title. Therefore, the learned Advocates sum up that, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court is absolutely based on proper appreciation and assessment of evidence on record and of law, and, therefore, they have prayed for discharging the Rule.

9. 1 have heard the learned Advocates for both the parties, perused the application for revision, lower Court's record as well as the judgment of both the Courts below and other materials on record.

10. 1 find that, during cross-examination of PW 1 (the sole-witness) he has admitted that Albela Khatun was alive, but, he could not produce his alleged foster mother Albela Khatun as witness to prove the oral gift said to have been made by her in his favour or to support his possession by making a shop in the suit property. The certificate issued by the concerned Chairman, No. I Rajanagar Union Parishad on 20-3-2008, is not a relevant document to prove either the case of oral gift or of possession, as claimed by the plaintiff. I also find that, during examination of PW 1, he has admitted possession of the defendant on the suit property by admitting that "না: দাগে বিবাদীদের ঘর-বাড়ি চিনি।"

11. Hence, the appellate court has rightly pointed out that, the plaintiff (petitioner) did not produce Albela Khatun to prove his case and that she was his foster mother. The appellate court has also recorded that, at the time of alleged oral gift and handing over of possession on 15-1-1974, Bochan Ali, Naderuzzaman, Kabir Ahmed and Bodiul Alam were present, as per plaintiff's narration of his case. But, having examined the record of Title Suit No. 94 of 2004, he has rightly found that, the plaintiff did neither call, nor examined any one of them as witness, to prove handing over of the possession of the suit property as alleged.

12. The defendant's case that, they have acquired the suit property from Albela Khatun on the basis of a registered sale deed No. 573 dated 17-3-2004 (Exhibit-Kha) has been duly proved by adducing the attesting witness (DW 2) and the genuineness, existence or execution of the exhibit Kha has not been challenged by the plaintiff.

13. Besides, I also find that, the appellate court has recorded the deposition of DW 2, who is the attesting witness No. 3 of the aforesaid sale deed No. 573 dated 17-3-2004 (Exhibit-Kha). On these points, the appellate court has found title and possession of the defendant in the suit property and held that, the findings of the trial court were not based on proper appreciation or assessment of the evidence on record. Hence, the appellate court has set-aside the finding of the trial court.

<u>14. The appellate court has rightly held that, no one can, in the absence of any lawful title, claim permanent injunction in the suit property, nor the plaintiff, having entered into the suit property on the basis of oral license can deny or refuse to hand over the possession of the suit property. The appellate court has correctly found that, the defendant had no legal interest in the suit property.</u>

<u>15. In 10 MLR (AD) 100: between Md Kamal vs AKM Mohsin in which, the Apex Court held that, in a suit for permanent injunction, if the dispute involves complicated question of title the plaintiff must establish his title by filing a regular suit for declaration of title. A simple suit for permanent injunction should not be allowed to be used as a testing devise for ascertainment of title.</u>

16. In view of the discourse made above, I hold that, the appellate court has committed no error of law in passing the impugned judgment and decree, nor the same has resulted in any error of law, nor it has occasioned any failure of justice.

17. I find no merit in this Rule and the same should be discharged.

Order

In the result, the Rule is discharged. The impugned judgment and decree dated 19-1-2017 (decree signed on 24-1-2017), passed by the Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Chattogram, in Other Appeal No.517 of 2011 is hereby affirmed.

The order of stay granted earlier by this Court is hereby vacated.

No costs.

Copies of this judgment along with the Lower Court's Record be sent down to the concerned Courts at once and another copy to the concerned Chairman, No. 1 Rajanagar Union Parishad, PO: Thandachari, Upzilla: Rangunia, Chattogram. Another copy of this judgment and order be sent to the Up-Zilla Nirbahi Officer, for recording the misconduct of this Union Parishad Chairman.

End.
